title: Infosys, TCS and Other IT Stocks Fall Up to 3% as Anthropic's IPO Filing Reprices AI
excerpt: Indian IT shares fell up to 3% on Tuesday as Anthropic's Nasdaq filing under the ticker ANT — $16.3 billion in half-year revenue and huge losses — lifted global AI and chip stocks while pressuring legacy services firms.
body:
• Indian IT stocks including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra fell up to 3% on Tuesday amid reports Anthropic is preparing an IPO that could value the Claude maker at around $1.5 trillion.
  • Anthropic filed an S-1 to list Class A shares on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT; revenue was $16.3 billion in the six months to June 30, 2026, up 1,300% year on year, against a net loss of $80.75 billion for the same period.
  • The same filing lifted AI hardware: Nvidia and Micron rose about 3% overnight, South Korea's KOSPI surged 5%, and SK Hynix rallied more than 8%.
  • For diaspora investors, the split is the story: model and chip companies are being repriced up while labour-led IT services are being repriced down.

India's information technology stocks fell on Tuesday as Anthropic's move toward a public listing forced investors to reprice who captures the value in artificial intelligence. Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra fell up to 3% amid reports that Anthropic, the maker of Claude, is preparing an initial public offering that could value the company at around $1.5 trillion, according to 24x7 Live News.

Anthropic has filed for an IPO under the ticker ANT and is preparing to market its shares, though the number of shares on offer and the price range have yet to be determined. The listing would give public-market investors direct exposure to one of the leading developers of AI models — and, as Tuesday's trade showed, it also sharpens the question hanging over services firms whose model is billing for human engineering hours.

What the filing disclosed

Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday for a proposed offering of Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Revenue was $41 million in 2023, $386 million in 2024 and $4.6 billion in 2025, and reached $16.3 billion in the six months ended June 30, 2026 — a year-over-year growth rate of 1,300 per cent, according to IANS via hi INDiA.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=nlGovMUBYFM

"We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all."

— Anthropic, in its S-1 filing

The losses are as striking as the growth: a net loss of $41.97 billion for 2025 and $80.75 billion for the first six months of 2026. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead a large underwriting syndicate that includes J.P. Morgan, Citigroup, Barclays and Wells Fargo Securities. Founded in 2021, Anthropic is a public benefit corporation; Claude runs on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure and is trained across Amazon Trainium, Google TPUs and Nvidia and AMD chips. The prospectus contains no specific disclosure on India-based operations or Indian customers.

Two trades in one filing

Overnight, the beneficiaries were hardware names: Nvidia and Micron closed about 3% higher, South Korea's KOSPI surged 5%, SK Hynix rallied more than 8% and Samsung gained 5%. The logic is symmetrical — every dollar of Anthropic-scale model training is a dollar of chip, memory and cloud demand, while every task Claude automates is a task a services firm once billed for.

That does not settle the longer argument. Indian IT firms are themselves selling AI implementation to the same clients, and a listed Anthropic at a trillion-dollar-plus valuation must eventually show a path from $80 billion half-year losses to cash flow. But on Tuesday the market's verdict was clear, and for the many diaspora households whose savings and salaries both run through Indian IT, it landed on both sides of the ledger at once.
